Directed false-positive review identifies a semantic-success proxy defect: all 20 muse-vision probes return HTTP 200 and the requested alias but have empty content, finish_reason=length and reasoning-only output. Thus successful_response_rate=1.0 proves transport success, not successful task completion across all six aliases.

Directed false-negative review finds no route-misbinding or deterministic-drift failure in the retained records. The operational route/transport result is strong, but fail-closed provenance prevents signing R1. The already-PROMOTED R2 successor rebinds the immutable retained source set and explicitly separates 120/120 transport integrity from 80/80 non-empty content on eligible text aliases; it supersedes R1 without retroactively curing its provenance or broad success proxy.
limitations: Artifact identity was recorded per route but was not freshly rehashed at every one of the 30 boundaries.
Text-only probes on vision aliases cannot establish vision capability, and empty muse-vision content cannot be interpreted as semantic success.
claim_boundary: No R1 claim code is authorized. The packet indicates only bounded routing, HTTP transport, alias identity and repeatability for the retained campaign; it does not establish semantic task success for all routes, vision quality, production readiness or behavior beyond the probes. BACKLOG-GATEWAY-ROUTE-STRESS-02 is the terminal rebound claim.
